 /**
  * Chrome Locale Runtime — interface (chrome) strings only.
  *
  * Per ADR docs/decisions/2026-06-21-chrome-locale-runtime-i18n.md and issue #3671.
  *
  * SCOPE BOUNDARY (immersion rule #M-13): this dictionary holds ONLY navigation /
  * UI chrome strings — the scaffolding that lets a learner operate the site. It
  * MUST NOT contain teaching content, dialogue, vocab glosses, primary-source
  * texts, work titles, author names, genre headers, lemmas, or attributions —
  * those are authored Ukrainian and stay Ukrainian regardless of this toggle.
  *
  * Default for this track (l2-uk-en = "Ukrainian for English speakers"): chrome
  * follows the user's own browser locale; English is the no-JS / non-`uk` fallback
  * so absolute beginners can navigate. Ukrainian chrome is auto-selected only for
  * `uk*` browsers, or chosen explicitly via the toggle. The LEARNING CONTENT is
  * always Ukrainian — this toggle never touches it.
  */
 
 export type ChromeLocale = 'uk' | 'en';
 
 /** No-JS / non-Ukrainian-browser fallback. See ADR "Default language". */
 export const DEFAULT_CHROME_LOCALE: ChromeLocale = 'en';

/** Both locale variants for a key — used by ChromeText for FOUC-safe dual-render. */
export function chromeBoth(key: ChromeKey): Record<ChromeLocale, string> {
  return { en: CHROME_STRINGS.en[key], uk: CHROME_STRINGS.uk[key] };
}

## What
C1 and C2 course pages are live on production (HTTP 200) but are not linked from header nav, footer, or the home Course Map. Words of the Day still exposes C1 and C2 level filters, so learners can hit those levels in one tool and not find the courses.

## Evidence (production QA, 2026-08-13)
- https://learn-ukrainian.github.io/c1/ → 200
- https://learn-ukrainian.github.io/c2/ → 200
- Home Course Map / header / footer: A1, A2, B1, B2 only
- https://learn-ukrainian.github.io/words-of-the-day/ level filter includes A1–C2

Seminar tracks (OES, RUTH, etc.) are already labeled planned / not promoted. C1/C2 may be the same on purpose.

## Options
1. Add C1/C2 to Course Map + nav (if they are ready to promote).
2. Keep them unlisted, but drop C1/C2 from Words of the Day (or mark those pages as unlisted/noindex) so the product surface matches.

## Notes
Not a 404. Flagging discoverability mismatch, not a content-complete claim.

The diff looks good. Let me also check the "Available Now" cards section — currently only A1-B2 cards. Should I add C1/C2 cards there? The issue is about nav + Course Map discoverability. The Course Map ladder section now lists C1/C2 with status "available". The roadmap panel includes C1/C2. Header nav + footer include them. 

Let me reconsider the "Available Now" cards. The B2 promotion added a B2 card. But C1/C2 have no released modules (0 available, all planned). Adding cards saying "available now" would be misleading. The Course Map ladder with "available" status is the right level of promotion since the landing pages are live but modules are planned. I'll leave the Available Now cards as-is (A1-B2 + reference tools) since C1/C2 modules aren't released.

Wait — actually, let me reconsider. The status.available means "available" which is in the course map ladder. That's good. But the roadmap panel now says "Advanced course map" / "Mastery course map". Good.

Now, one concern: the `state: 'released'` for c1/c2 in TRACKS. The `state` field isn't consumed anywhere at render (I checked earlier). It's only used in the type. But `heroVariant: 'core'` matters — for the `track` kind route (when no landingDoc exists), it renders hero. But since c1/c2 have index.mdx landingDocs, the `landingDoc` kind is used, not `track`. So `heroVariant` is only used in pageMeta for landingDoc via `TRACKS[track]?.heroVariant ?? 'core'`. Let me verify that. Actually for landingDoc, pageMeta uses `heroVariant: TRACKS[track]?.heroVariant ?? 'core'`. And showHero={props.kind !== 'landingDoc' && props.kind !== 'track'} → false for landingDoc. So hero isn't shown for landingDocs. Good — the LevelLanding component renders its own hero.

Let me double check the c1/c2 landing docs use `template: splash` and render LevelLanding directly. Yes, from c1/index.mdx: `import LevelLanding from '@site/src/components/LevelLanding'` and renders it. So `[...slug].astro` for c1/c2 uses kind 'landingDoc' → renders `<Content />`. The TRACKS c1/c2 entries are only used for search index text (searchItems) and pageTrack/meta fallback. Since landingDocs exist, the search items text will now say "Live course map" instead of "Planned / unavailable". Good — search results will be honest.

Let me verify the search index output in the built dist to confirm.
The diff is clean and focused. Let me verify the search index text for C1/C2 in the built output reflects the live state, and double-check the words-of-the-day page nav.
